title.from: The home page sends visitors to their language, and their choice sticks
title.to: A countdown banner welcomes visitors into their language on any translated page

description.from:
As a visitor, I want the bare home page to open in my browser's preferred language unless I have chosen one, and my choice to stick, while search engines always see the primary home page.

Design: only '/' is ever redirected, never article pages. In the existing CloudFront viewer-request function: '?lang=xx' sets papyrus_lang and redirects to that language's clean home; then the cookie; then Accept-Language matched to public languages; no header or no match means no redirect. Redirects are 302, Cache-Control private, no-store, Vary Accept-Language, Cookie; page cache keys and page responses unchanged. No user-agent sniffing, no client-side redirect. Off by default for primary-at-root sites (opt-in setting); always on for prefixed sites. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Home-page language

Scenario: A Spanish-preferring visitor lands on the English root
  Given Machines on Machines has the home redirect on and Spanish public
  And a visitor whose browser prefers Spanish has made no choice
  When they open the root
  Then they are redirected to /es/ and the redirect is not cached

Scenario: A visitor's choice sticks
  Given a visitor whose browser prefers Spanish
  When they choose English in the language switcher
  Then the root opens in English on every later visit

Scenario: A crawler is not redirected
  Given a request for the root with no Accept-Language header
  When it reaches the site
  Then the English home page is served

Scenario: Article pages are never redirected
  Given a visitor whose browser prefers Spanish
  When they open an English article link
  Then the English article is served with a link to its Spanish version if one exists
description.to:
As a visitor, I want any page that also exists in my browser's preferred language to offer that version with a short, friendly countdown, and my choice to be remembered, so I read in my language without being nagged.

Design (Ryan's decision 6, revised): client-side only, no server redirect, no Vary, no cookie; the CloudFront-function redirect is removed from the design. Applies to home, listings, articles and wiki pages, only when that exact page exists in the preferred language (from the page's hreflang links); no banner otherwise. Banner in the visitor's language: 15-second countdown with progress bar, Switch now, Stay here, Pause; scrolling, typing or selecting text pauses it; announced once with aria-live polite; reduced motion removes the animation; keyboard reachable without moving focus; lang set on its text. Switching uses location.replace (no Back loop). Reading language remembered in localStorage, set only by the visitor's actions (switch, countdown finished, stay, undo, switcher); later pages in another language switch at once with a quiet 'Switched to 中文 · Undo' note; pages not in the reading language do nothing. The countdown never switches toward the site's primary language (search renderers run timers with an English preference); a quiet 'Read in English' link is shown instead. Off switch per site (languages.switchBanner), default on. GA4 language_switch event. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450), revised 2026-11-12 with Ryan's decisions.

Feature: Welcoming language switch

Scenario: A Chinese reader opens a shared English article that has a Chinese version
  Given an English article with a published Chinese localization
  And a visitor whose browser prefers Chinese and who has made no choice
  When they open the English article from a shared link
  Then a banner in Chinese says the Chinese version will open in 15 seconds
  And it offers Switch now, Stay here and Pause
  And when the countdown ends the Chinese article replaces the English one in the browser history

Scenario: No banner when the page has no translation
  Given an English article with no Chinese localization
  And a visitor whose browser prefers Chinese
  When they open the article
  Then no banner appears

Scenario: Starting to read pauses the countdown
  Given the banner is counting down
  When the visitor scrolls the article
  Then the countdown stops and the banner keeps Switch now and Stay here

Scenario: The choice is remembered on later pages
  Given a visitor who switched to Chinese once
  When they open another English page that has a Chinese version
  Then the Chinese page opens at once with a quiet note offering Undo

Scenario: A visitor who stays is not asked again
  Given a visitor whose browser prefers Chinese chose Stay here on an English page
  When they open other English pages that have Chinese versions
  Then no banner appears

Scenario: Back does not loop
  Given a visitor arrived from search results and was switched to Chinese
  When they press Back
  Then they return to the search results

Scenario: Never counting down toward the primary language
  Given a Spanish article on a site whose primary language is English
  And a visitor whose browser prefers English
  When they open the Spanish article
  Then a quiet Read in English link appears and no countdown runs

Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given a visitor who prefers reduced motion
  When the banner appears
  Then the number counts down in text without an animated bar
